body: @jmartisk does it work outside of Quarkus? I think it's something that should be supported.
I just tried the same with Thorntail and it works correctly there, it seems we might need a change in Quarkus. Let me have a look what can be done.

The problem seems to be related to the fact that metric interceptors in SmallRye Metrics have `@AroundInvoke` methods that are `private` (in the case of counters: https://github.com/smallrye/smallrye-metrics/blob/1.1.3/implementation/src/main/java/io/smallrye/metrics/interceptors/CountedInterceptor.java#L62). 

In Quarkus, it seems that when a REST endpoint is intercepted by such interceptor, and the endpoint throws an exception, and the interceptor simply rethrows it, then the exception gets wrapped in a `RuntimeException` here:  https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/0.12.0/independent-projects/arc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/arc/Reflections.java#L114

But then it is no longer a `NotFoundException` but rather a `RuntimeException` so it is not mapped to 404 but to 500 by RESTEasy.

@mkouba , is this the correct behavior that an exception gets wrapped into a `RuntimeException` if it is rethrown by an interceptor with a private `@AroundInvoke`? In Thorntail the exception seems to stay as it is. Perhaps the `Reflections` class, if it receives an `InvocationTargetException`, should unwrap the original exception from inside it? 

If that can't be done, we would need to fix this by making the interceptors in SR-M `public`.

@jmartisk +1 for unwrapping the original exception. Feel free to send a PR! ;-)

Anyway, changing the interceptor methods to package-private would not hurt too. I see no real value in having them `private`.

issue.title: Avoid wrapping runtime exceptions between interceptors in some cases
Get rid of private interceptor methods
issue.body: This can be problematic for Quarkus (see for example https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/1668) and is not good practice in general, it was suggested that we make all interceptor methods package-private instead.
